implemented_claims: A strict `oya gate validate cloud-iac-module-catalog` lane now exists and is registered in the run-all gate catalog.
The gate validates Cloud IaC manifest catalog path, source root, module count, module names, and modeled registry fields against the local catalog.

The gate validates catalog schema_version, catalog_id slug, authority source root, non-empty non-claims, module identity fields, exact semver, OpenTofu system, repo-relative paths, source_path/main_file shape, duplicate release keys, local skeleton honesty flags, evidence_ref shape, and on-disk `main.tofu` existence.
Cloud IaC manifest now declares this gate-backed local filesystem/JSON guard while preserving runtime/provider/module-signing non-claims.
explicit_non_claims: No live OpenTofu private module registry API is implemented.
No module signing/cosign attestation, provider mirror, provider dependency lockfile, provider credential, or provider-resource-complete module body is implemented.
No tofu init, validate, test, plan, apply, drift detection, REST, SDK, worker, provider adapter, rollback engine, or Argo CD API integration is implemented.
No measured SLO, active-active DR, sharding execution, mesh runtime enforcement, or capacity telemetry readiness is claimed.
false_green_findings_closed: Manifest module_count/module_names can no longer drift from the catalog without failing a first-class Oya gate.
Catalog entries can no longer point to missing `main.tofu` files without failing a first-class Oya gate.
Local skeleton entries can no longer claim provider resources, materialized outputs, or tests without failing the gate.
The run-all catalog now includes the Cloud IaC catalog coherence lane, so the previous custom evidence-time check is no longer the only enforcement path.
known_gaps: This is a local filesystem/JSON coherence gate, not a live registry service.
The gate intentionally does not execute OpenTofu or validate provider lockfiles/checksums.
Legacy Cloud IaC Markdown/IP/capability prose may still contain future-state planning language and remains de-authorized by manifest non-claims.
Live registry/runtime/provider/OpenTofu/Argo CD work remains sequentially blocked behind future contract slices.

findings: The implementation is a narrow local validator rather than a broad registry/runtime stack.
It uses existing serde_json in oya-dev-cli and avoids adding dependencies or widening the pure domain crate.
The gate locks shared IaC catalog truth before downstream cloud write fanout.
It uses OpenTofu module identity shape while explicitly refusing live/provider/runtime readiness claims.

A live registry API requires contracts, persistence, auth, release signing, and runtime evidence beyond this sequential slice.
